title: India's Music Economy Generated Rs 17,401 Crore in Gross Value in 2025, EY Finds
excerpt: The EY-IPRS report puts economy-wide music value up 45% since 2023, with independent music at 43% of digital consumption — while direct recording and publishing revenue was Rs 5,433 crore and only 55% of surveyed authors earn full-time from music.
body:
• Music generated Rs 17,401 crore (about $1.8 billion) in gross economic value in India in 2025, up 45% from Rs 12,047 crore in 2023, according to a new EY report backed by the Indian Performing Right Society.
  • That headline figure is economy-wide value — digital platforms, broadcasting, concerts and filmed entertainment — not label revenue: sound recording and publishing together earned Rs 5,433 crore.
  • Independent music accounted for 43% of digital music consumption in 2025, up from 37% in 2024 and under 35% in 2023.
  • India logged nearly 6 trillion streams in 2025, but only 14.4 million of its roughly 233 million music streamers pay for a subscription.

India's music economy generated Rs 17,401 crore in gross economic value in 2025, about $1.8 billion, rising 45% from Rs 12,047 crore in 2023, according to It is a Good Time to Be in Music: India's Music Creator Economy Report Vol. 2, a new EY study backed by the Indian Performing Right Society (IPRS) and reported by Exchange4Media and Loudest.

What the $1.8 billion actually counts

The headline number is gross value across the wider ecosystem, and the report's breakdown matters more than the total. Digital platforms contributed 52% of the value, broadcasting 21%, concerts and events 16%, and filmed entertainment 11%. The narrower, direct music business — sound recording and publishing, including licensing and other income — earned Rs 5,433 crore in 2025, a record high of about $563 million, up 7% from Rs 5,086 crore in 2024. Within that, music publishing and performance revenues grew from Rs 628 crore in 2023 to Rs 1,125 crore in 2025. EY projects the recording and publishing segment to reach Rs 7,160 crore by 2028, a projection of about 10% compound annual growth, not a reported result.

"India's music economy is creating significant value, but its long-term success will be measured by how effectively that value reaches creators."

— Ashish Pherwani, Partner and Media & Entertainment Leader, EY India

Independent music's rising share

Independent music — regional artists building audiences through social media, live performance and digital distribution outside the traditional film and label system — accounted for 43% of digital music consumption in India in 2025, up from 37% in 2024 and under 35% in 2023, on EY estimates based on IPRS data. Half of Spotify India's Top 10 songs in 2025 were from independent artists. By language, Hindi accounted for 59% of consumption, down from 64% in 2024, followed by Punjabi at 9%, Tamil at 7% and Telugu at 6%.

Huge listening, thin paying base

India logged nearly 6 trillion streams in 2025, roughly 16.4 billion a day, across about 233 million music streamers. Paying subscribers rose from 7 million in 2023 to 14.4 million in 2025, but that is a paid penetration of about 6%, against 45% in the US and 50% in the UK on the report's comparison, and about 97% of streams remain free or ad-supported. EY forecasts paid subscribers reaching 28 to 30 million by 2028. Live music is expanding faster: about 130 concert days in 2025 drew more than 10,000 attendees a day, up from about 70 days in 2024.

The creator gap

The report's caution is about who captures the value. Of more than 1,000 music authors surveyed by IPRS and EY, 85% said they want to live exclusively from music, but only 55% do so full-time, down from 60% in the 2023 survey; 75% believed opportunities are increasing, while 76% felt it is becoming harder to take advantage of them. Publishing compliance — usage actually reported and paid — stood at 4.1% in 2025, up from 1.2% in 2023, and 10 to 12% of songs remain unmatched because of inadequate metadata. The organised segment employs an estimated 60,000 to 70,000 people, and IPRS membership has grown from 13,500 in 2023 to more than 23,500 in 2025. What to watch is whether the forecast growth in paid subscriptions and publishing collections closes the gap between the economy's headline value and creators' incomes.
nri_angle: Indian music's growth is increasingly driven by independent regional artists and streaming, the same catalogue diaspora listeners consume abroad; 19% of streams of Indian music on the platforms IPRS tracked were generated outside India.
author: Diaspora Desk
